questions_used.question: All 23 relations, or the main paths?
questions_used.answer: All of them. Every relation once. I'd rather navigate a big canvas than lose a path.

questions_used.question: One canvas or several separate panes?
questions_used.answer: One canvas with everything, split into named diagrams I can read. Describe each one so I know what I'm looking at.

questions_used.question: Motion?
questions_used.answer: Slow, sparse dots — one per live transition. Nothing on the historical ones, and no dot sitting on a border.

questions_used.question: Which concepts separate into diagrams, and on what seam?
questions_used.answer: Three described diagrams on the source's own clusters: request+provisioning (control-plane gRPC, webapi, River queue, provider registry, providers, machines, boot server, S3), heartbeat+machine state (agent, public gRPC, Postgres and the other two Postgres writers), slow ops+reconcile (SSH audits, janitor, webapi to Slack, one-minute gcore sync). No component is unique to a fourth cluster, and a fourth diagram would be a two-edge fragment.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — source.md names its three edge groups itself ("Request path (provisioning)", "Heartbeat path (fastest)", "Ops path (slow)"), and the brief asks for named, described sections; the split follows those three groups verbatim.

questions_used.question: Are provider registry and machine-agent grouped, drawn as their own boxes, or dropped?
questions_used.answer: Both are drawn as their own boxes with group tags (provider registry: control, machine-agent: hardware) and both keep every relation they own in the source.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — the brief allows grouping but forbids dropping, and source.md lists both as nodes with edges of their own; a group tag is the least lossy way to satisfy both.

questions_used.question: Do both machines -> boot and boot -> machines survive, and is the queue -> S3 diagnostics edge kept apart from the machine image pull?
questions_used.answer: Yes: R8 'iPXE request' and R9 'boot.ipxe + S3 args' are two separately labelled routes in the request diagram; O6 'diagnose uploads' (queue -> S3) sits in the ops diagram, in a different section from R10 'pull boot image' (machines -> S3).
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — fixed constraints in source.md, checked by the relationship audit below.

questions_used.question: Which hops are historical, so they carry no dot?
questions_used.answer: None is marked historical in source.md, so no relation is muted on that ground. Exactly one relation is dot-free: H1 machines -> machine-agent 'runs on host', which is a residency fact, not a live transition.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — source.md qualifies no relation as historical/unconfirmed and describes every other relation as a moving action or message; the source's own correction ('use way less dots. keep on dot alive per line') and its constraint ('slow, sparse dots on selected communication edges') both point at communication, and 'runs on host' communicates nothing.

triage.converged_when: After the three annex answers plus the Q4-Q7 judgments: scope (all 17 components, all 23 relations), shape (one canvas of described diagrams), seam (the source's three named paths), coverage qualifiers (both boot directions, the separate queue -> S3 diagnostics, registry/agent never dropped) and motion (one constant-speed dot per live transition, none on the residency edge) were all fixed. No remaining question could change the drawing, so triage stopped.

classification.evidence: One River job queue state fans to 5 destinations (provider registry, Postgres, SSH+BMC ops, janitor, S3) and the source marks every transition live ('keep on dot alive per line'), so one dot per line.
tie_breakers_considered: Density: E=23 > N=17, so it is not a flow-chain (E≈N) even though several of its paths are chains.
No source-named shared bus between weakly connected worlds, so it is not placement-planes; the phases connect through the queue, the database and the providers.
Identifier density is low (verbs and payloads, few addresses), so it is not an identity-probe-map.
classification.secondary_recipe: service-meshes: its anti-parallel-pair habit was borrowed for machines <-> boot server, which stay in ONE diagram as two labelled routes with distinct ports (R8/R9) instead of being split.

view_shape.rung_label: one large canvas hosting several concept-diagrams, each with a drawn title and one-line description
deciding_source_facts: 17 components and 23 directed relations; a 7-rank request chain (cp -> pgrpc -> q -> reg -> prov -> mch -> boot) alone is 260 cells wide at natural zoom with its 17-22 character labels.
The source groups its own relations into three named paths (request/provisioning, heartbeat/fastest, ops/slow), each a separate concept a reader can name.
The brief states the reader's job is navigational ('where does this path go?') and asks for named, described sections.
Round 12's honest measurement of the same facts as one flat graph was 101x136 - larger than the 77x47 pane on both axes.

diagrams.title: Request and provisioning path
diagrams.description: Humans and the control plane enter through webapi and private gRPC, enqueue River jobs, and provision bare metal down to the iPXE boot.

diagrams.title: Heartbeat and machine state
diagrams.description: The fastest path: each host's machine-agent registers and heartbeats over public gRPC. Public gRPC, private gRPC and the queue each write their own Postgres rows.

diagrams.title: Slow ops path and reconcile loop
diagrams.description: Queued work beside the fast path: SSH audits, diagnostics to the janitor, its proposals through webapi to Slack, and the one-minute gcore cluster sync.

known_defects.defect: The canvas is 260x64, so no pane at 77x47 can show it whole; the reader pans. The request section is a 260x11 ribbon (3.4 pane widths).
known_defects.why_it_stands: Its 7-rank chain with 17-22 character source labels does not shrink honestly: top-to-bottom cost 150 rows (c1), label_slot gutters cost routing (c3: 6 near-miss cells, 2 ambiguous labels, 1 skipped label). Left-to-right was the only clean option.

known_defects.defect: The viewer's controls legend (and, when the drawing overflows, its minimap) is painted over the canvas at the viewport's bottom corners, so on any pane smaller than the canvas it overwrites drawing cells.
known_defects.why_it_stands: Viewer chrome, not a spec property (rataflow/src/lib.rs draw_frame renders Controls and MiniMap after the canvas); the spec cannot move a section out of the corner. In the 68x44 pane the legend covers the first 11 cells of the ops title (evidence/canvas/canvas-text.txt, last 8 rows) and in the 300x18 request window it covers part of the 'humans + mmctl' label (evidence/canvas/sections/request-300x18-frames.txt rows 8-13, cols 1-10). At 300x70, where the whole canvas fits, the legend falls on the empty left margin only (evidence/canvas/canvas-300x70-frames.txt rows 63-69).
